title: Talking Someone Through a Problem: The Full Advice Toolkit

sections.title: Four lessons, one conversation
sections.content: Talking a friend through a real dilemma usually needs several of this unit's tools working together in one conversation: imagining yourself in their place (a helyedben / ha ... lennék), floating options gently (-hat/-het + conditional), weighing them out loud (egyrészt... másrészt...), and warning about a genuine risk with care rather than alarm (nehogy, -hat/-het for a possible bad outcome).

sections.title: The toolkit at a glance
rows: in your place / if I were...
it'd be better if... / you'd better...
on one hand... on the other hand...

sections.title: Talking a friend through a dilemma

items.spanish: Szerintem most tanácstalan vagy, de ez nem baj.
items.english: I think you're at a loss right now, but that's okay.

items.spanish: A helyedben én először mérlegelném az előnyöket és a hátrányokat.
items.english: In your place, I'd weigh the advantages and disadvantages first.

items.spanish: Egyrészt biztonságosabb maradni, másrészt izgalmasabb lenne váltani.
items.english: On one hand it's safer to stay, on the other hand it'd be more exciting to switch.

items.spanish: Nehogy siess a döntéssel — előbb beszélhetnél egy tanácsadóval is.
items.english: Don't rush the decision — you could talk to an advisor first, too.

items.spanish: De végül a döntés a tiéd — én csak elmondtam, mit tennék a helyedben.
items.english: But in the end the decision is yours — I've just told you what I would do in your place.

sections.content: Notice what all five tools have in common: none of them decides for the other person. Hungarian advice-giving language is built to hand the final choice back — that pragmatic habit matters just as much as any single grammar point in this unit.
